Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__read_documentation
tools.description: The documentation for the machine and product this session runs in: a claude.ai cloud container and the settings around it (GitHub access, connectors, the environment's secrets, network access, setup script and installed tools, the session's limits and permission prompts, Remote Control). Read it whenever something about your container or environment comes up, whether it blocked you, you worked around it, or the person asked how to set it up. For example: the repository the work is about is not in your container, a clone or push is refused, a service you need has no connected connector, an outbound host is denied, a command-line tool is missing, you need an API key, the person asks how to stop permission prompts. Read it rather than answering from memory because these settings move and get renamed faster than your training data, and a page says what is true now: the current steps, where in the product the person makes the change, and what you can do yourself. Reading a page also helps the person directly: in the Claude Code app they see a card with a button that takes them to that settings page, so they can fix it themselves while you carry on. Call it with no topic to list the pages and when each applies; call it with a topic to read that page. Read a page each time a different topic comes up; one read per topic is enough. It is read-only and needs no approval. It has nothing on bugs in the code you are working on.

The call returns when the message is delivered, not when it is answered; the target can reply with its own send_message, which arrives here as a new turn. Use this for meta-orchestration — e.g. asking a sibling session to perform a subtask.

The ts of the message from your principal that this answers: copy it from that message's <standing_owner_message ts="..."> envelope attribute (e.g. "1700000000.000200"). The server verifies it is one of your principal's own messages, then threads your reply under it. tools.name: mcp__hearthbot__mark_draft_sent
tools.description: Mark a draft on a draft card (a card whose widget name begins message_compose) as sent, so that an app that shows marks stops offering to send it and shows the user that you say you sent it. Call it after each drafted message that you have actually sent, whether the user pressed Send on the card or asked you in words, and never before: a mark cannot be taken off. The server takes a mark only once the user has written or pressed after the card was posted, in the chat or thread where the card is. The call sends nothing and does not change the draft, and a mark never means that the user approved a send. This call's answer lists the card's marked drafts under marked_drafts, by their numbers as you pass them. A card's body, read with full_bodies true, lists them under agent_marked_sent in another way: that list does not hold the numbers that you pass as draft. It holds positions in the card's variants list, counted from 0: 0 is the first entry of variants and 1 the second, whatever numbers the entries carry. So after a call with draft 1 on a card that numbers its drafts 1, 2 and 3, the body's list holds 0.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

"
I'll start the deep research sweep now, covering the literature, prior work, where the gaps are, and a full dry-lab plan for the thesis.

Your precision fermentation thesis blueprint and prior-art assessment is ready. It confirms your topic is novel as an integrated computational (dry-lab) thesis—no published work spans all five target proteins (casein, β-lactoglobulin, α-lactalbumin, ovalbumin, leghemoglobin) across K. phaffii and T. reesei in a single in-silico pipeline. The report includes a prior-art map showing which computational pieces already exist, a quantified breakdown of the folding/PTM/downstream-cost challenges (with the casein phosphorylation/micelle problem as your centerpiece), peer-reviewed titer and techno-economic benchmarks, and sustainability LCA ranges with caveats. It culminates in a concrete chapter-by-chapter ~60-page blueprint using only free, laptop-friendly tools (AlphaFold2/ColabFold, GROMACS+MARTINI, SignalP/DeepLoc, COBRApy, spreadsheet TEA), plus recommendations to frame the work as a comparative "tractability ranking" of the five proteins.


# Precision Fermentation Microbial Cell Factories for Animal-Free Dairy, Heme and Alternative Proteins: A Computational Thesis Blueprint and Prior-Art Assessment

## TL;DR

- **Your topic is real, hot and well-sourced — but it has not been done as a single computational (dry-lab) thesis, which is exactly your opening.** The science (Perfect Day's β-lactoglobulin in *Trichoderma reesei*, Impossible Foods' soy leghemoglobin in *Komagataella phaffii*) is commercially established, and individual computational pieces exist (AlphaFold on casein, molecular dynamics on casein micelles, flux-balance models of *K. phaffii*, codon-optimization tools), but no published thesis integrates all five target proteins across an end-to-end in-silico pipeline. Position the thesis as a *novel integration*, not a new wet-lab discovery.

These numbers give your FBA and techno-economic chapters concrete anchors.
- **Downstream purification is the cost driver.** Chromatography is designed for high-purity, high-value pharma products and is too expensive for bulk food proteins; reviews call for cheaper precipitation/membrane routes.\[14\] A demonstrated example: β-lactoglobulin from *P. pastoris* purified by polyphosphate precipitation raised protein content from 26 to 72 wt% with emulsification preserved (Hoppenreijs et al., *Food Research International*, 2024, 176:113801).\[15\] Yeast mannan/extracellular polysaccharide interference is a named purification obstacle for *K. phaffii* proteins.

### 3. Economic and sustainability context (for your introduction/discussion)

- **Sustainability is the headline selling point, with caveats.** The WSP USA LCA for Perfect Day (2021), ISO 14067-conformant and reviewed by an independent expert panel, reports (per the combined ISO-conformant report) GHG emissions "between 91.2% and 96.6% lower" than total protein in bovine milk (the standalone GHG report states 85–97%), with blue water 96–99% lower and non-renewable energy 29–60% lower. GFI's synthesis of 30+ LCAs gives similar ranges. But some peer-reviewed work (e.g., Behm et al., 2022) finds fermentation proteins can have *higher* emissions than efficient dairy systems depending on the electricity mix, and an Imperial College London analysis stresses that land-use savings (up to ~96%) are more robust than carbon savings. Present the ranges honestly, not as settled fact.
- **Cost is the make-or-break variable.** Public techno-economic estimates for precision-fermented protein span an enormous and under-informative range — GFI found four public models ranging from under $20/kg to roughly $15,000/kg. A 2025 GFI Europe / Arthur D. Little model put food-grade α-lactalbumin near $24/kg and high-purity grades near $100/kg; secondary industry sources cite current commodity-protein COGS of $10–50/kg with projections toward $8–12/kg at >100,000 L scale. For context, commodity whey protein is ~$2–8/kg. The target benchmark cited by GFI is that commodity precision-fermentation proteins must reach under $20/kg to compete.
- **The sector is real but funding tightened.** The GFI 2026 State of the Industry (Fermentation) report states: "Companies operating primarily in the fermentation ecosystem raised $357 million in 2025, according to GFI analysis of data from Net Zero Insights (down from $632 million in 2024)." FDA clearances accelerated: by late 2025 multiple companies held GRAS "no questions" letters across whey (Perfect Day GRN 863; Imagindairy/Remilk GRN 1056-type; Vivici's Vivitein BLG), egg white (The EVERY Company GRN 1104/1249;\[16\] Onego Bio's Bioalbumen, Sept 2025), lactoferrin (TurtleTree's LF+, March 2025), and casein (New Culture, self-affirmed). Verley became the first to get an FDA "no questions" letter for precision-fermented dairy protein in October 2025. This gives your thesis a current, well-documented commercial backdrop.

## Details: A Chapter-by-Chapter Thesis Blueprint (laptop-only)

The following is a concrete ~60-page structure. Every method is free or has a free tier and runs on a personal computer (some steps use free cloud GPUs via Google Colab).

**Front matter + Chapter 1 — Introduction (~6–8 pp).** Define precision fermentation; contrast with traditional fermentation; state the recombinant-DNA core idea; introduce the five targets (casein, β-lactoglobulin/whey, ovalbumin, soy leghemoglobin, lactoferrin) and the two hosts (*K. phaffii*, *T. reesei*). State the thesis question: *which animal-free proteins are most computationally tractable to produce, and what does in-silico analysis predict about the folding, PTM, secretion, metabolic and cost bottlenecks?* Include the Arabic abstract.

**Chapter 2 — Literature review & prior-art map (~10 pp).** Synthesize the reviews above; build a table of companies, proteins, hosts, titers and regulatory status; explicitly document that the individual computational pieces exist but the integrated pipeline does not. This chapter alone satisfies the "search whether someone has already done this" requirement and justifies novelty.

**Chapter 3 — Target selection & sequence/bioinformatics analysis (~8 pp).** Retrieve sequences from UniProt (e.g., bovine β-casein P02666, κ-casein P02668,\[17\] β-lactoglobulin P02754, α-lactalbumin P00711, hen ovalbumin P01012, soybean leghemoglobin LGB2, human/bovine lactoferrin). Tools: UniProt, NCBI, Clustal/MUSCLE alignments, Protter for topology, and disorder predictors (IUPred, metapredict) to show caseins are intrinsically disordered. Deliverable: a cross-species comparison and a quantified PTM-dependency table.

**Chapter 4 — Structure prediction & folding analysis (~8–10 pp).** Run AlphaFold2 via ColabFold (free Colab GPU) and, where accessible, AlphaFold3 for each target. Report pLDDT and PAE; show that globular whey proteins predict with high confidence while caseins yield low-pLDDT disordered models — a result you can interpret as the "folding/disorder challenge." Caveat clearly (cite the 2025 bioRxiv work showing\[18\] AlphaFold3 is reliable for disordered monomers but unreliable for disordered multimers). Deliverable: annotated predicted structures and a confidence comparison.

**Chapter 5 — The casein phosphorylation & micelle bottleneck via molecular dynamics (~8–10 pp, the novel core).** Using AlphaFold casein models, build coarse-grained MARTINI simulations in GROMACS to study κ/β-casein self-assembly, following the published PLOS ONE 2025 workflow. Compare phosphorylated vs. dephosphorylated serine states and their effect on calcium-phosphate-mediated aggregation, connecting to the nanocluster model of the micelle (Holt; de Kruif). This directly addresses the slide's "correct PTM" challenge with original simulation output. Keep scope realistic — short CG trajectories, not microsecond atomistic runs.

**Chapter 6 — Gene design: codon optimization & secretion (~6 pp).** Codon-optimize each target for *K. phaffii* using host-specific tools: Pichia-CLM (a 2026 language-model optimizer trained on the *K. phaffii* genome), ICOR (open-source RNN optimizer, noting it is *E. coli*-trained and needs caution), and Codon Pair Optimization. Compare CAI, GC content and codon-pair bias before/after. Predict secretion with SignalP 6.0 and DeepLoc 2.0, testing the α-mating-factor leader vs. native signals. Deliverable: optimized constructs and predicted secretion efficiency.

**Chapter 7 — Host metabolic modeling with flux-balance analysis (~6–8 pp).** Download a published *K. phaffii* genome-scale model (iMT1026/iMT1026v3 from BioModels, Kp.1.0, or the 2026 iPichia/ecPichia consensus/enzyme-constrained models) and run simulations in COBRApy with the free GLPK solver. Add a recombinant-protein "demand" reaction; use FBA/FSEOF to estimate metabolic burden on glycerol vs. methanol, and identify over-expression/knockout targets — especially the heme-pathway flux limits relevant to leghemoglobin. Deliverable: predicted growth-vs-production trade-offs and gene targets, mirroring the published Acharya 2026 bottleneck workflow.

**Chapter 8 — Techno-economic & sustainability modeling (~6 pp).** Build a transparent spreadsheet (or free SuperPro trial) model of fed-batch fermentation + chromatography-free downstream (centrifugation, micro/ultrafiltration, spray-dry), parameterized with the titers from Chapter 2 (1 g/L BLG, 3.5 g/L LegH, 1.2 g/L lactoferrin). Produce $/kg sensitivity to titer, yield and purification choice, and summarize the LCA ranges with their caveats. Deliverable: a cost model showing why titer and downstream dominate, consistent with published TEA.

**Chapter 9 — Integrated tractability ranking, discussion, limitations, future wet-lab validation (~6 pp).** Combine all chapters into a single scored ranking of the five proteins; state limitations (prediction ≠ experiment; AlphaFold disorder caveats; model-dependent FBA/TEA); propose the minimal wet-lab experiments that would validate the top prediction.

## Recommendations

1. **Adopt the comparative "tractability ranking of five proteins" as your thesis spine.** It is original, it directly answers the slide's challenge, it is impossible to scoop with a single prior paper, and it naturally fills ~60 pages without a bench.
2. **Make the casein phosphorylation/micelle molecular-dynamics chapter your centerpiece of originality.** It is the hardest, most-cited bottleneck, and the AlphaFold→MARTINI→GROMACS workflow is already published and reproducible, so you are building on solid ground rather than inventing a method.
3. **Lead with *K. phaffii* as your primary chassis** because it has the richest free tooling (host-specific codon models, multiple downloadable genome-scale metabolic models, well-characterized secretion signals) and is the host for leghemoglobin and ovalbumin; treat *T. reesei* as the secondary/comparison host for whey.
4. **Report ranges, not point values, for sustainability and cost, and flag the dissenting LCAs.** This protects your scientific credibility and shows examiner-pleasing epistemic maturity.
5. **Keep every computational scope deliberately modest and pre-register it** (sequence sets, simulation lengths, model versions) so the project "finishes correctly and takes its proper time," per your stated priority over novelty.
6. **Verify the newest tools before committing** — Pichia-CLM, ecPichia/iPichia and the GitHub FBA repo are all dated 2026; download and test-run them early, and have fallbacks (standard CAI optimization, iMT1026, Kp.1.0) in case a tool is unavailable.

## Caveats

- **Computational predictions are hypotheses, not proof.** AlphaFold confidence for intrinsically disordered caseins is intrinsically limited, FBA predicts capability not actual flux, and techno-economic models carry wide uncertainty (the public range spans under $20/kg to ~$15,000/kg). Frame every result as predictive and clearly state assumptions.
- **Some of the most useful sources are preprints, company LCAs or trade press** (bioRxiv, Perfect Day's own LCA, market-research pages, GFI). Prefer the peer-reviewed anchors (Annual Reviews, *Food Research International*, *Bioresource Technology*, *Trends in Biotechnology*) for load-bearing claims and label the rest as industry/preliminary.
- **Titer figures evolve fast.** The 1 g/L BLG and 2 g/L ovalbumin numbers are 2023 research-scale benchmarks; Yao, Zhu, An, Zhang, Zheng & Cai, Food Bioscience vol. 82, art. 109383 (Aug 2026) report "a final titer of 13.88 g/L in bioreactor fermentation… the reported highest titer for heterologous β-LG expression in yeast so far" in Komagataella phaffii, and companies claim far higher (e.g.,\[19\] ~120 g/L ovalbumin) — treat company numbers as unverified claims and cite the peer-reviewed figure as your baseline.
- **Tool access and compute limits are real.** AlphaFold3 and some MD runs need GPU time; plan around free Colab quotas, keep simulations short, and document hardware so results are reproducible on a student machine.
- **This report is a research-and-design assessment, not a guarantee of results.** The actual simulation and modeling outputs will depend on your parameter choices; the value of the thesis lies in doing the integration carefully and transparently, exactly as your constraints prioritize.

# Titer database extraction spec (v1)

All literature extraction writes **one TSV row per reported titer measurement** (not per paper).
File: `data/literature/titers_<batch>.tsv`. Header exactly as below, tab-separated, no quoting.

| column | meaning | rules |
|---|---|---|
| `record_id` | `<batch>-<n>` | unique within batch |
| `protein_name` | common name | e.g. `beta-lactoglobulin`, `bovine alpha-s1-casein` |
| `uniprot` | accession of the mature protein expressed | `NA` if not determinable; give best guess + note |
| `source_organism` | organism the gene came from | e.g. `Bos taurus`, `Glycine max` |
| `host_species` | expression host | `Komagataella phaffii`, `Trichoderma reesei`, `Saccharomyces cerevisiae`, ... |
| `host_strain` | strain if given | e.g. `GS115`, `X-33`, `CBS7435`, `QM9414` |
| `promoter` | e.g. `pAOX1`, `pGAP`, `pcbh1` | `NA` if unstated |
| `signal_peptide` | e.g. `alpha-MF`, `native`, `CBHI-carrier` | `NA` |
| `copy_number` | integer or `NA` | |
| `localisation` | `secreted` / `intracellular` | |
| `cultivation` | `shake_flask` / `fedbatch_bioreactor` / `batch_bioreactor` / `microscale` | |
| `carbon_source` | `glycerol`, `methanol`, `glycerol+methanol`, `glucose`, `lactose`, ... | |
| `titer_mg_L` | numeric, mg/L | convert g/L x1000; if a range, use the max and note it |
| `titer_basis` | `total_secreted_protein` / `target_protein_quantified` / `activity_inferred` | |
| `quantification` | `SDS-PAGE densitometry`, `ELISA`, `HPLC`, `BCA`, `LC-MS`, `heme assay`, ... |
| `volumetric_productivity_mg_L_h` | numeric or `NA` | |
| `year` | publication year |
| `doi` | DOI, or `NA` |
| `pmid` | PMID, or `NA` |
| `reference` | `FirstAuthor et al., Journal Year` |
| `evidence_quote` | <=240 chars, verbatim sentence containing the number |
| `confidence` | `high` (peer-reviewed, explicit number, clear units) / `medium` (inferred/derived) / `low` (preprint, company claim, abstract only) |
| `notes` | anything else material |

## Hard rules
1. **Never invent a number.** If a DOI/PMID can't be confirmed, set it `NA` and lower `confidence`.
2. `evidence_quote` must be text you actually read on the page you fetched. If you could only read an abstract, say so in `notes`.
3. Company press claims are allowed but must be `confidence=low` and `notes` must say `company_claim`.
4. Prefer **secreted, target-protein-quantified, bioreactor** rows; but record shake-flask rows too (they are usable with a cultivation covariate).
5. Record **every** independent titer in a paper (different strains/promoters/copy numbers = different rows).
6. Also write `data/literature/papers_<batch>.tsv` with: `doi`, `pmid`, `year`, `title`, `journal`, `url`, `relevance` (`titer`/`method`/`background`/`prior_art`), `one_line_finding`.

You are auditing the novelty of a specific research claim. Be adversarial: your job is to find the work that would scoop it, not to reassure.

THE CLAIM TO BE AUDITED: that a *stoichiometry-grounded, sequence-informed "producibility index" for recombinant food proteins* in Komagataella phaffii and Trichoderma reesei is novel. The intended method: (1) compute each target protein's exact metabolic cost from its amino-acid composition using a genome-scale metabolic model — ATP/NADPH burden and maximum theoretical g protein per g glycerol/methanol; (2) compute a sequence-feature panel (intrinsic disorder, phosphorylation motifs, N/O-glycosylation sequons, disulfide count, codon adaptation, signal-peptide/secretion prediction, aggregation propensity); (3) fit a model that predicts published secretion titers from those features and says which bottleneck binds for each protein.

AUDIT THESE LITERATURES SYSTEMATICALLY, and for each say plainly whether it scoops, partially overlaps, or is merely adjacent:
1. **Amino-acid / protein biosynthetic cost**: Akashi & Gojobori 2002; Barton/Wagner cost studies; Kaleta et al. metabolic cost of amino acids; Lynch & Marinov energetic cost of a gene; "proteome allocation cost", "ATP cost per peptide bond".
2. **Protein cost in genome-scale models**: protein-synthesis demand reactions, ME-models (iJL1678b-ME), GECKO/ecModels, resource-allocation models, "cost of recombinant protein production flux balance analysis", yeast/Pichia-specific recombinant-protein FBA (including the iMT1026, Kp1.0, iPichia/ecPichia lineage, and the kphaffii-metabolic-bottlenecks GitHub project).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fetch target protein sequences + annotation from UniProt REST.

Writes:
  data/sequences/targets.json   full records (sequence, features, PTMs)
  data/sequences/targets.fasta  mature-chain-annotated fasta
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "sequences")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

# name -> uniprot accession.  Chosen for food-protein relevance + benchmark calibration.
TARGETS = {
    # bovine caseins
    "alpha_s1_casein_bovine": "P02662",
    "alpha_s2_casein_bovine": "P02663",
    "beta_casein_bovine": "P02666",
    "kappa_casein_bovine": "P02668",
    "beta_casein_human": "P05814",
    "kappa_casein_human": "P07498",
    # bovine whey
    "beta_lactoglobulin_bovine": "P02754",
    "alpha_lactalbumin_bovine": "P00711",
    "alpha_lactalbumin_human": "P00709",
    "lactoferrin_bovine": "P24627",
    "lactoferrin_human": "P02788",
    "lactoperoxidase_bovine": "P80025",
    "osteopontin_bovine": "P31096",
    "serum_albumin_bovine": "P02769",
    "serum_albumin_human": "P02768",
    # egg white
    "ovalbumin_chicken": "P01012",
    "ovotransferrin_chicken": "P02789",
    "ovomucoid_chicken": "P01005",
    "avidin_chicken": "P02701",
    "lysozyme_c_chicken": "P00698",
    "cystatin_chicken": "P01038",
    # heme proteins
    "leghemoglobin_c2_soybean": "P02234",
    "leghemoglobin_a_soybean": "P02232",
    "myoglobin_bovine": "P02192",
    "myoglobin_pig": "P02189",
    "hemoglobin_alpha_human": "P69905",
    "hemoglobin_beta_human": "P68871",
    # benchmark / calibration proteins with well-documented Pichia or Trichoderma titers
    "chymosin_bovine": "P00794",
    "human_growth_hormone": "P01241",
    "insulin_human": "P01308",
    "trypsin_porcine": "P00761",
    "phytase_aspergillus_niger": "P34752",
    "cbhi_cel7a_trichoderma": "P62694",
    "xylanase_ii_trichoderma": "P36217",
    "glucoamylase_aspergillus_niger": "P69328",
    "hsa_domain_free_control": "P02768",
}

FIELDS = ",".join([
    "accession", "id", "protein_name", "organism_name", "sequence", "length",
    "mass", "ft_signal", "ft_chain", "ft_disulfid", "ft_mod_res",
    "ft_carbohyd", "ft_propep", "cc_ptm", "ft_transmem", "ft_region",
])


def fetch(acc, tries=4):
    url = (f"https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/{acc}.json")
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as fh:
                return json.load(fh)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            sys.stderr.write(f"  retry {i+1} {acc}: {e}\n")
            time.sleep(3 * (i + 1))
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed {acc}")


def main():
    recs = {}
    for name, acc in TARGETS.items():
        print(f"fetch {name} ({acc})", flush=True)
        d = fetch(acc)
        seq = d["sequence"]["value"]
        feats = d.get("features", [])

        def of(ftype):
            out = []
            for f in feats:
                if f["type"] != ftype:
                    continue
                loc = f["location"]
                out.append({
                    "start": loc["start"].get("value"),
                    "end": loc["end"].get("value"),
                    "desc": f.get("description", ""),
                })
            return out

        recs[name] = {
            "name": name,
            "accession": acc,
            "uniprot_id": d.get("uniProtkbId"),
            "protein_name": (d.get("proteinDescription", {})
                             .get("recommendedName", {})
                             .get("fullName", {}).get("value")),
            "organism": d.get("organism", {}).get("scientificName"),
            "sequence": seq,
            "length": d["sequence"]["length"],
            "mass_da": d["sequence"].get("molWeight"),
            "signal": of("Signal"),
            "propeptide": of("Propeptide"),
            "chain": of("Chain"),
            "disulfide": of("Disulfide bond"),
            "mod_res": of("Modified residue"),
            "carbohyd": of("Glycosylation"),
            "transmem": of("Transmembrane"),
        }
        time.sleep(0.3)

    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "targets.json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(recs, fh, indent=1)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "targets.fasta"), "w") as fh:
        for n, r in recs.items():
            fh.write(f">{n}|{r['accession']}|{r['organism']}\n")
            s = r["sequence"]
            for i in range(0, len(s), 60):
                fh.write(s[i:i + 60] + "\n")
    print(f"\nwrote {len(recs)} records")
    for n, r in recs.items():
        print(f"  {n:38s} {r['accession']}  L={r['length']:5d}  "
              f"SP={len(r['signal'])} SS={len(r['disulfide'])} "
              f"MOD={len(r['mod_res'])} GLY={len(r['carbohyd'])}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                if f["type"] != ftype:
                    continue
                loc = f["location"]
                out.append({
                    "start": loc["start"].get("value"),
                    "end": loc["end"].get("value"),
                    "desc": f.get("description", ""),
                })
            return out

        recs[name] = {
            "name": name,
            "accession": acc,
            "uniprot_id": d.get("uniProtkbId"),
            "protein_name": (d.get("proteinDescription", {})
                             .get("recommendedName", {})
                             .get("fullName", {}).get("value")),
            "organism": d.get("organism", {}).get("scientificName"),
            "sequence": seq,
            "length": d["sequence"]["length"],
            "mass_da": d["sequence"].get("molWeight"),
            "signal": of("Signal"),
            "propeptide": of("Propeptide"),
            "chain": of("Chain"),
            "disulfide": of("Disulfide bond"),
            "mod_res": of("Modified residue"),
            "carbohyd": of("Glycosylation"),
            "transmem": of("Transmembrane"),
        }
        time.sleep(0.3)

    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "targets.json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(recs, fh, indent=1)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "targets.fasta"), "w") as fh:
        for n, r in recs.items():
            fh.write(f">{n}|{r['accession']}|{r['organism']}\n")
            s = r["sequence"]
            for i in range(0, len(s), 60):
                fh.write(s[i:i + 60] + "\n")
    print(f"\nwrote {len(recs)} records")
    for n, r in recs.items():
        print(f"  {n:38s} {r['accession']}  L={r['length']:5d}  "
              f"SP={len(r['signal'])} SS={len(r['disulfide'])} "
              f"MOD={len(r['mod_res'])} GLY={len(r['carbohyd'])}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stoichiometric cost of recombinant protein synthesis and secretion.

Builds, for an arbitrary amino-acid sequence, an explicitly mass- and
electron-balanced synthesis reaction that can be inserted into a genome-scale
metabolic model (GEM).  The reaction accounts for

  1. amino-acid draw (every residue translated, including the signal peptide),
  2. translational energy (aminoacyl-tRNA charging + elongation, in ATP
     equivalents),
  3. oxidative folding (disulfide formation via Ero1/PDI, electrons to O2),
  4. N-glycosylation (sugar-nucleotide donors for the yeast core glycan plus
     outer-chain mannose),
  5. O-mannosylation (Dol-P-Man donors),
  6. serine/threonine phosphorylation (kinase ATP), used for the caseins,
  7. haem b prosthetic group (globins),
  8. chaperone (BiP/Kar2) ATPase cycles,
  9. vesicular transport GTP (COPII/COPI/Rab),
 10. signal-peptide cleavage with optional amino-acid recycling.

All parameters live in `CostParams` so that every number in the paper can be
traced to a citation and varied in sensitivity analysis.

References for the default parameter values are in
`docs/COST_PARAMETERS.md`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Residue chemistry
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# free amino acid elemental composition (neutral, zwitterion-free formula)
AA_FORMULA: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {
    "A": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "R": {"C": 6, "H": 14, "N": 4, "O": 2},
    "N": {"C": 4, "H": 8, "N": 2, "O": 3},
    "D": {"C": 4, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 4},
    "C": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 2, "S": 1},
    "Q": {"C": 5, "H": 10, "N": 2, "O": 3},
    "E": {"C": 5, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 4},
    "G": {"C": 2, "H": 5, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "H": {"C": 6, "H": 9, "N": 3, "O": 2},
    "I": {"C": 6, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "L": {"C": 6, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "K": {"C": 6, "H": 14, "N": 2, "O": 2},
    "M": {"C": 5, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2, "S": 1},
    "F": {"C": 9, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "P": {"C": 5, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "S": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "T": {"C": 4, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "W": {"C": 11, "H": 12, "N": 2, "O": 2},
    "Y": {"C": 9, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "V": {"C": 5, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2},
}

# model metabolite id (cytosolic) for each residue, as used by iMT1026v3
AA_MET: Dict[str, str] = {
    "A": "ala_L_c", "R": "arg_L_c", "N": "asn_L_c", "D": "asp_L_c",
    "C": "cys_L_c", "Q": "gln_L_c", "E": "glu_L_c", "G": "gly_c",
    "H": "his_L_c", "I": "ile_L_c", "L": "leu_L_c", "K": "lys_L_c",
    "M": "met_L_c", "F": "phe_L_c", "P": "pro_L_c", "S": "ser_L_c",
    "T": "thr_L_c", "W": "trp_L_c", "Y": "tyr_L_c", "V": "val_L_c",
}

ATOMIC_MASS = {"C": 12.0107, "H": 1.00794, "N": 14.0067, "O": 15.9994,
               "S": 32.065, "P": 30.973762, "Fe": 55.845}

H2O = {"H": 2, "O": 1}
HPO3 = {"H": 1, "O": 3, "P": 1}          # phosphoryl group added by a kinase
GLCNAC_RES = {"C": 8, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 5}   # GlcNAc residue (-H2O)
MAN_RES = {"C": 6, "H": 10, "O": 5}              # hexose residue (-H2O)
HAEM_B = {"C": 34, "H": 30, "Fe": 1, "N": 4, "O": 4}   # protoheme, as in model


def _add(a: Dict[str, float], b: Dict[str, float], n: float = 1.0) -> None:
    for k, v in b.items():
        a[k] = a.get(k, 0.0) + n * v


def formula_mass(f: Dict[str, float]) -> float:
    return sum(ATOMIC_MASS[k] * v for k, v in f.items())


def formula_str(f: Dict[str, float]) -> str:
    out = []
    for k in ("C", "H", "N", "O", "P", "S", "Fe"):
        if f.get(k):
            v = f[k]
            v = int(round(v)) if abs(v - round(v)) < 1e-6 else round(v, 4)
            out.append(f"{k}{v}")
    return "".join(out)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class CostParams:
    """Every tunable number in the cost model.

    Defaults are the literature-canonical values; see docs/COST_PARAMETERS.md.
    """

    # --- translation -------------------------------------------------------
    atp_per_residue: float = 4.3
    """ATP equivalents consumed per residue polymerised.

    2 per aminoacyl-tRNA charging (ATP -> AMP + PPi, i.e. two high-energy
    phosphate bonds) + 1 GTP for eEF1A delivery + 1 GTP for eEF2 translocation
    = 4; the extra 0.3 covers initiation, termination and proofreading/
    mischarging, and is the value used in the yeast GEM lineage.
    """
    initiation_atp: float = 2.0
    """ATP equivalents per chain for initiation + termination + release."""

    # --- signal peptide ----------------------------------------------------
    include_signal_peptide: bool = True
    """Translate the signal peptide (it is always synthesised before cleavage)."""
    recycle_signal_peptide: bool = True
    """Return the cleaved signal-peptide residues as free amino acids.

    Signal-peptide peptidase and the cytosolic peptidases that clear the
    fragment are ATP-independent, so recycling is the conservative choice; it
    makes the net amino-acid draw equal to the mature chain while the
    translational energy is still paid for the full precursor.
    """

    # --- oxidative folding -------------------------------------------------
    o2_per_disulfide: float = 1.0
    """O2 consumed per disulfide bond formed.

    One disulfide = 2 electrons; Ero1p passes them through FAD to O2 in a
    two-electron step giving H2O2, so 1 O2 -> 1 H2O2 per disulfide.
    """
    isomerisation_cycles_per_disulfide: float = 0.0
    """Futile reduction/re-oxidation cycles per disulfide (NADPH via GSH).

    Baseline 0 (perfect folding on the first pass); raised in the
    misfolding-burden scenarios.
    """

    # --- N-glycosylation ---------------------------------------------------
    n_glycan_mannose: float = 9.0
    """Mannose residues retained per N-glycan.

    K. phaffii transfers Glc3Man9GlcNAc2 and trims to Man8GlcNAc2, then
    extends with alpha-1,2 and alpha-1,6 outer-chain mannose; secreted
    recombinant glycoproteins carry predominantly Man8-Man14. 9 is the
    central value; 5 models a glyco-engineered (humanised) strain and 14 the
    hypermannosylated extreme.
    """
    n_glycan_glcnac: float = 2.0
    n_glycan_transient_glucose: float = 3.0
    """Glc residues added to the dolichol precursor and later trimmed.

    They are paid for even though they do not end up on the protein; the free
    glucose released is returned to the cytosol.
    """
    recycle_transient_glucose: bool = True

    # --- O-mannosylation ---------------------------------------------------
    o_mannose_per_site: float = 2.0
    """Mannose residues per O-mannosylated Ser/Thr in K. phaffii (1-5)."""

    # --- phosphorylation ---------------------------------------------------
    atp_per_phosphorylation: float = 1.0
    phosphorylate: bool = False
    """Whether the host is engineered to phosphorylate the target.

    False for wild-type K. phaffii / T. reesei, which do not phosphorylate
    casein; True in the PTM-competent scenario.
    """

    # --- chaperones and traffic -------------------------------------------
    bip_atp_per_residue: float = 0.0
    """BiP/Kar2 ATPase cycles per residue, as ATP equivalents.

    Baseline 0 so that the stoichiometric floor is a strict lower bound on
    cost; raised in the folding-burden scenarios, where it is the term that
    couples sequence features to metabolic cost.
    """
    transport_gtp_per_molecule: float = 6.0
    """GTP for COPII budding, COPI retrieval and Rab/Ypt cycles per molecule."""

    # --- prosthetic groups -------------------------------------------------
    haem_per_molecule: float = 0.0
    """Protoheme b per protein molecule (1 for monomeric globins)."""


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sequence feature extraction
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

import re

SEQUON = re.compile(r"N[^P][ST]")


def count_sequons(seq: str) -> int:
    """N-X-S/T sequons, X != P, counted with overlap."""
    return sum(1 for i in range(len(seq) - 2) if SEQUON.match(seq, i))


def sequon_positions(seq: str) -> List[int]:
    return [i + 1 for i in range(len(seq) - 2) if SEQUON.match(seq, i)]


@dataclass
class ProteinSpec:
    """What the cost model needs to know about one protein."""
    name: str
    sequence: str                 # full precursor, signal peptide included
    signal_end: int = 0           # 1-based last residue of the signal peptide
    n_disulfide: int = 0
    n_sequon: Optional[int] = None        # default: computed from mature chain
    n_o_glyc_site: int = 0
    n_phosphosite: int = 0
    n_haem: int = 0
    accession: str = ""
    notes: str = ""

    @property
    def mature(self) -> str:
        return self.sequence[self.signal_end:]

    @property
    def signal(self) -> str:
        return self.sequence[:self.signal_end]

    def sequons(self) -> int:
        if self.n_sequon is not None:
            return self.n_sequon
        return count_sequons(self.mature)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cost computation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class CostResult:
    name: str
    length_precursor: int
    length_mature: int
    # the product
    product_formula: Dict[str, float]
    product_mass_da: float
    # per molecule
    aa_draw: Dict[str, float]            # residue letter -> count (net)
    atp: float
    gtp: float
    o2: float
    h2o2: float
    nadph: float
    gdpmann: float
    uacgam: float
    udpg: float
    dolmanp: float
    haem: float
    # derived
    carbon_in_product: float
    carbon_in_precursors: float
    atp_per_g: float = 0.0
    nadph_per_g: float = 0.0
    carbon_per_g: float = 0.0
    breakdown: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)


def compute_cost(spec: ProteinSpec, p: CostParams) -> CostResult:
    seq_full = spec.sequence
    seq_mat = spec.mature
    Lp, Lm = len(seq_full), len(seq_mat)

    # --- amino-acid draw --------------------------------------------------
    charged = seq_full if p.include_signal_peptide else seq_mat
    draw: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for a in charged:
        if a in AA_MET:
            draw[a] = draw.get(a, 0.0) + 1.0
    if p.include_signal_peptide and p.recycle_signal_peptide:
        for a in spec.signal:
            if a in AA_MET:
                draw[a] -= 1.0

    # --- product elemental formula (mature, modified chain) ---------------
    f: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for a in seq_mat:
        if a in AA_FORMULA:
            _add(f, AA_FORMULA[a])
    _add(f, H2O, -(Lm - 1))                 # peptide bonds
    n_ss = float(spec.n_disulfide)
    _add(f, {"H": -2.0 * n_ss})             # 2 H lost per disulfide
    n_seq = float(spec.sequons())
    _add(f, GLCNAC_RES, p.n_glycan_glcnac * n_seq)
    _add(f, MAN_RES, p.n_glycan_mannose * n_seq)
    _add(f, MAN_RES, p.o_mannose_per_site * spec.n_o_glyc_site)
    n_phos = float(spec.n_phosphosite) if p.phosphorylate else 0.0
    _add(f, HPO3, n_phos)
    n_haem = float(spec.n_haem) if spec.n_haem else p.haem_per_molecule
    _add(f, HAEM_B, n_haem)
    mass = formula_mass(f)

    # --- energy -----------------------------------------------------------
    atp_translation = p.atp_per_residue * Lp + p.initiation_atp
    atp_bip = p.bip_atp_per_residue * Lp
    atp_phos = p.atp_per_phosphorylation * n_phos
    atp = atp_translation + atp_bip + atp_phos
    gtp = p.transport_gtp_per_molecule

    # --- redox ------------------------------------------------------------
    o2 = p.o2_per_disulfide * n_ss
    h2o2 = o2
    nadph = p.isomerisation_cycles_per_disulfide * n_ss

    # --- glycan donors ----------------------------------------------------
    uacgam = p.n_glycan_glcnac * n_seq
    # core mannose up to Man5 comes straight from GDP-Man on the cytosolic
    # face; the rest is delivered as Dol-P-Man.
    core_direct = min(p.n_glycan_mannose, 5.0) * n_seq
    via_dolmanp = max(p.n_glycan_mannose - 5.0, 0.0) * n_seq \
        + p.o_mannose_per_site * spec.n_o_glyc_site
    gdpmann = core_direct + via_dolmanp     # Dol-P-Man itself is made from GDP-Man
    dolmanp = via_dolmanp
    udpg = p.n_glycan_transient_glucose * n_seq

    # --- carbon accounting -------------------------------------------------
    c_prod = f.get("C", 0.0)
    c_prec = sum(AA_FORMULA[a]["C"] * n for a, n in draw.items() if n > 0)
    c_prec += 6 * (gdpmann + udpg) + 8 * uacgam + 34 * n_haem

    r = CostResult(
        name=spec.name, length_precursor=Lp, length_mature=Lm,
        product_formula=f, product_mass_da=mass, aa_draw=draw,
        atp=atp, gtp=gtp, o2=o2, h2o2=h2o2, nadph=nadph,
        gdpmann=gdpmann, uacgam=uacgam, udpg=udpg, dolmanp=dolmanp,
        haem=n_haem, carbon_in_product=c_prod, carbon_in_precursors=c_prec,
    )
    g = mass / 1e3            # mmol-scale: 1 mmol protein = mass/1000 g
    r.atp_per_g = atp / g
    r.nadph_per_g = nadph / g
    r.carbon_per_g = c_prec / g
    r.breakdown = {
        "atp_translation": atp_translation,
        "atp_chaperone": atp_bip,
        "atp_phosphorylation": atp_phos,
        "gtp_transport": gtp,
        "o2_disulfide": o2,
        "nadph_isomerisation": nadph,
        "gdpmannose_glycan": gdpmann,
        "udpglcnac_glycan": uacgam,
        "udpglucose_transient": udpg,
        "haem": n_haem,
        "n_sequon": n_seq,
        "n_disulfide": n_ss,
        "n_phosphosite": n_phos,
    }
    return r


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GEM reaction construction
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_reactions(model, spec: ProteinSpec, p: CostParams,
                    rxn_prefix: str = "PROT_"):
    """Add synthesis + secretion reactions for `spec` to a cobra `model`.

    Returns (cost_result, synthesis_reaction, sink_reaction).
    The model is modified in place; wrap in `with model:` to undo.
    """
    import cobra

    r = compute_cost(spec, p)
    tag = rxn_prefix + spec.name

    prot_c = cobra.Metabolite(f"{tag}_c", name=f"{spec.name} (cytosol/secreted)",
                              compartment="c",
                              formula=formula_str(r.product_formula))

    stoich = {}

    def add(met_id, coeff):
        if coeff == 0:
            return
        m = model.metabolites.get_by_id(met_id)
        stoich[m] = stoich.get(m, 0.0) + coeff

    for a, n in r.aa_draw.items():
        add(AA_MET[a], -n)

    # translational and chaperone energy, as ATP equivalents
    add("atp_c", -r.atp)
    add("h2o_c", -r.atp)
    add("adp_c", r.atp)
    add("pi_c", r.atp)
    add("h_c", r.atp)

    # vesicular transport GTP
    add("gtp_c", -r.gtp)
    add("h2o_c", -r.gtp)
    add("gdp_c", r.gtp)
    add("pi_c", r.gtp)
    add("h_c", r.gtp)

    # water released by peptide-bond formation (mature chain)
    add("h2o_c", r.length_mature - 1)
    # water released when the signal peptide is hydrolysed off and recycled
    if p.include_signal_peptide and p.recycle_signal_peptide and spec.signal_end:
        add("h2o_c", -spec.signal_end)

    # oxidative folding
    add("o2_c", -r.o2)
    add("h2o2_c", r.h2o2)
    # futile isomerisation: NADPH -> NADP+ via glutathione reductase
    if r.nadph:
        add("nadph_c", -r.nadph)
        add("h_c", -r.nadph)
        add("nadp_c", r.nadph)
        # the electrons end up reducing O2 as well
        add("o2_c", -0.5 * r.nadph)
        add("h2o_c", r.nadph)

    # N- and O-glycan donors
    add("uacgam_c", -r.uacgam)
    add("udp_c", r.uacgam)
    add("gdpmann_c", -r.gdpmann)
    add("gdp_c", r.gdpmann)
    add("udpg_c", -r.udpg)
    add("udp_c", r.udpg)
    if p.recycle_transient_glucose and r.udpg:
        add("glc_D_c", r.udpg)

    # phosphorylation
    if r.breakdown["n_phosphosite"]:
        # ATP already charged above as ATP equivalents; the phosphoryl group
        # transferred to the protein must not also leave as free phosphate.
        add("pi_c", -r.breakdown["n_phosphosite"])

    # haem b
    if r.haem:
        if "pheme_c" not in model.metabolites:
            hm = model.metabolites.get_by_id("pheme_m")
            hc = cobra.Metabolite("pheme_c", name="Protoheme", compartment="c",
                                  formula=hm.formula)
            model.add_metabolites([hc])
            tr = cobra.Reaction("PHEMEtm", name="Protoheme mitochondrial export")
            tr.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
            tr.add_metabolites({hm: -1.0, hc: 1.0})
            model.add_reactions([tr])
        add("pheme_c", -r.haem)

    stoich[prot_c] = stoich.get(prot_c, 0.0) + 1.0

    rxn = cobra.Reaction(tag, name=f"{spec.name} synthesis and secretion")
    rxn.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
    model.add_reactions([rxn])
    rxn.add_metabolites(stoich)

    sink = cobra.Reaction("EX_" + tag, name=f"{spec.name} secretion (exchange)")
    sink.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
    model.add_reactions([sink])
    sink.add_metabolites({prot_c: -1.0})

    return r, rxn, sink


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loading the target panel
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def specs_from_uniprot_json(path: str,
                            phospho_from_annotation: bool = True
                            ) -> Dict[str, ProteinSpec]:
    with open(path) as fh:
        recs = json.load(fh)
    out = {}
    for name, d in recs.items():
        sp_end = d["signal"][0]["end"] if d["signal"] else 0
        n_ss = len(d["disulfide"])
        phos = 0
        o_gly = 0
        n_gly_ann = 0
        for m in d["mod_res"]:
            if "Phospho" in (m["desc"] or ""):
                phos += 1
        for c in d["carbohyd"]:
            desc = (c["desc"] or "")
            if desc.startswith("N-linked"):
                n_gly_ann += 1
            elif desc.startswith("O-linked"):
                o_gly += 1
        haem = 1 if ("globin" in name or "hemoglobin" in name) else 0
        out[name] = ProteinSpec(
            name=name, sequence=d["sequence"], signal_end=sp_end,
            n_disulfide=n_ss, n_o_glyc_site=o_gly,
            n_phosphosite=phos if phospho_from_annotation else 0,
            n_haem=haem, accession=d["accession"],
            notes=f"uniprot_Nglyc_annotated={n_gly_ann}",
        )
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    specs = specs_from_uniprot_json(
        os.path.join(here, "..", "data", "sequences", "targets.json"))
    p = CostParams()
    print(f"{'protein':38s} {'Lmat':>5s} {'SS':>3s} {'Nseq':>4s} {'P':>3s} "
          f"{'kDa':>7s} {'ATP/mol':>8s} {'ATP/g':>8s} {'C/g':>7s}")
    for n, s in sorted(specs.items()):
        r = compute_cost(s, p)
        print(f"{n:38s} {r.length_mature:5d} {int(s.n_disulfide):3d} "
              f"{int(s.sequons()):4d} {int(s.n_phosphosite):3d} "
              f"{r.product_mass_da/1000:7.2f} {r.atp:8.0f} "
              f"{r.atp_per_g:8.1f} {r.carbon_per_g:7.1f}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stoichiometric cost of recombinant protein synthesis and secretion.

Builds, for an arbitrary amino-acid sequence, an explicitly mass- and
electron-balanced synthesis reaction that can be inserted into a genome-scale
metabolic model (GEM).  The reaction accounts for

  1. amino-acid draw (every residue translated, including the signal peptide),
  2. translational energy (aminoacyl-tRNA charging + elongation, in ATP
     equivalents),
  3. oxidative folding (disulfide formation via Ero1/PDI, electrons to O2),
  4. N-glycosylation (sugar-nucleotide donors for the yeast core glycan plus
     outer-chain mannose),
  5. O-mannosylation (Dol-P-Man donors),
  6. serine/threonine phosphorylation (kinase ATP), used for the caseins,
  7. haem b prosthetic group (globins),
  8. chaperone (BiP/Kar2) ATPase cycles,
  9. vesicular transport GTP (COPII/COPI/Rab),
 10. signal-peptide cleavage with optional amino-acid recycling.

All parameters live in `CostParams` so that every number in the paper can be
traced to a citation and varied in sensitivity analysis.

References for the default parameter values are in
`docs/COST_PARAMETERS.md`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Residue chemistry
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# free amino acid elemental composition (neutral, zwitterion-free formula)
AA_FORMULA: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {
    "A": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "R": {"C": 6, "H": 14, "N": 4, "O": 2},
    "N": {"C": 4, "H": 8, "N": 2, "O": 3},
    "D": {"C": 4, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 4},
    "C": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 2, "S": 1},
    "Q": {"C": 5, "H": 10, "N": 2, "O": 3},
    "E": {"C": 5, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 4},
    "G": {"C": 2, "H": 5, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "H": {"C": 6, "H": 9, "N": 3, "O": 2},
    "I": {"C": 6, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "L": {"C": 6, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "K": {"C": 6, "H": 14, "N": 2, "O": 2},
    "M": {"C": 5, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2, "S": 1},
    "F": {"C": 9, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "P": {"C": 5, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 2},
    "S": {"C": 3, "H": 7, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "T": {"C": 4, "H": 9, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "W": {"C": 11, "H": 12, "N": 2, "O": 2},
    "Y": {"C": 9, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 3},
    "V": {"C": 5, "H": 11, "N": 1, "O": 2},
}

# model metabolite id (cytosolic) for each residue, as used by iMT1026v3
AA_MET: Dict[str, str] = {
    "A": "ala_L_c", "R": "arg_L_c", "N": "asn_L_c", "D": "asp_L_c",
    "C": "cys_L_c", "Q": "gln_L_c", "E": "glu_L_c", "G": "gly_c",
    "H": "his_L_c", "I": "ile_L_c", "L": "leu_L_c", "K": "lys_L_c",
    "M": "met_L_c", "F": "phe_L_c", "P": "pro_L_c", "S": "ser_L_c",
    "T": "thr_L_c", "W": "trp_L_c", "Y": "tyr_L_c", "V": "val_L_c",
}

ATOMIC_MASS = {"C": 12.0107, "H": 1.00794, "N": 14.0067, "O": 15.9994,
               "S": 32.065, "P": 30.973762, "Fe": 55.845}

H2O = {"H": 2, "O": 1}
HPO3 = {"H": 1, "O": 3, "P": 1}          # phosphoryl group added by a kinase
GLCNAC_RES = {"C": 8, "H": 13, "N": 1, "O": 5}   # GlcNAc residue (-H2O)
MAN_RES = {"C": 6, "H": 10, "O": 5}              # hexose residue (-H2O)
HAEM_B = {"C": 34, "H": 30, "Fe": 1, "N": 4, "O": 4}   # protoheme, as in model


def _add(a: Dict[str, float], b: Dict[str, float], n: float = 1.0) -> None:
    for k, v in b.items():
        a[k] = a.get(k, 0.0) + n * v


def formula_mass(f: Dict[str, float]) -> float:
    return sum(ATOMIC_MASS[k] * v for k, v in f.items())


def formula_str(f: Dict[str, float]) -> str:
    out = []
    for k in ("C", "H", "N", "O", "P", "S", "Fe"):
        if f.get(k):
            v = f[k]
            v = int(round(v)) if abs(v - round(v)) < 1e-6 else round(v, 4)
            out.append(f"{k}{v}")
    return "".join(out)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class CostParams:
    """Every tunable number in the cost model.

    Defaults are the literature-canonical values; see docs/COST_PARAMETERS.md.
    """

    # --- translation -------------------------------------------------------
    atp_per_residue: float = 4.3
    """ATP equivalents consumed per residue polymerised.

    2 per aminoacyl-tRNA charging (ATP -> AMP + PPi, i.e. two high-energy
    phosphate bonds) + 1 GTP for eEF1A delivery + 1 GTP for eEF2 translocation
    = 4; the extra 0.3 covers initiation, termination and proofreading/
    mischarging, and is the value used in the yeast GEM lineage.
    """
    initiation_atp: float = 2.0
    """ATP equivalents per chain for initiation + termination + release."""

    # --- signal peptide ----------------------------------------------------
    include_signal_peptide: bool = True
    """Translate the signal peptide (it is always synthesised before cleavage)."""
    recycle_signal_peptide: bool = True
    """Return the cleaved signal-peptide residues as free amino acids.

    Signal-peptide peptidase and the cytosolic peptidases that clear the
    fragment are ATP-independent, so recycling is the conservative choice; it
    makes the net amino-acid draw equal to the mature chain while the
    translational energy is still paid for the full precursor.
    """

    # --- oxidative folding -------------------------------------------------
    o2_per_disulfide: float = 1.0
    """O2 consumed per disulfide bond formed.

    One disulfide = 2 electrons; Ero1p passes them through FAD to O2 in a
    two-electron step giving H2O2, so 1 O2 -> 1 H2O2 per disulfide.
    """
    isomerisation_cycles_per_disulfide: float = 0.0
    """Futile reduction/re-oxidation cycles per disulfide (NADPH via GSH).

    Baseline 0 (perfect folding on the first pass); raised in the
    misfolding-burden scenarios.
    """

    # --- N-glycosylation ---------------------------------------------------
    n_glycan_mannose: float = 9.0
    """Mannose residues retained per N-glycan.

    K. phaffii transfers Glc3Man9GlcNAc2 and trims to Man8GlcNAc2, then
    extends with alpha-1,2 and alpha-1,6 outer-chain mannose; secreted
    recombinant glycoproteins carry predominantly Man8-Man14. 9 is the
    central value; 5 models a glyco-engineered (humanised) strain and 14 the
    hypermannosylated extreme.
    """
    n_glycan_glcnac: float = 2.0
    n_glycan_transient_glucose: float = 3.0
    """Glc residues added to the dolichol precursor and later trimmed.

    They are paid for even though they do not end up on the protein; the free
    glucose released is returned to the cytosol.
    """
    recycle_transient_glucose: bool = True

    # --- O-mannosylation ---------------------------------------------------
    o_mannose_per_site: float = 2.0
    """Mannose residues per O-mannosylated Ser/Thr in K. phaffii (1-5)."""

    # --- phosphorylation ---------------------------------------------------
    atp_per_phosphorylation: float = 1.0
    phosphorylate: bool = False
    """Whether the host is engineered to phosphorylate the target.

    False for wild-type K. phaffii / T. reesei, which do not phosphorylate
    casein; True in the PTM-competent scenario.
    """

    # --- chaperones and traffic -------------------------------------------
    bip_atp_per_residue: float = 0.0
    """BiP/Kar2 ATPase cycles per residue, as ATP equivalents.

    Baseline 0 so that the stoichiometric floor is a strict lower bound on
    cost; raised in the folding-burden scenarios, where it is the term that
    couples sequence features to metabolic cost.
    """
    transport_gtp_per_molecule: float = 6.0
    """GTP for COPII budding, COPI retrieval and Rab/Ypt cycles per molecule."""

    # --- prosthetic groups -------------------------------------------------
    haem_per_molecule: float = 0.0
    """Protoheme b per protein molecule (1 for monomeric globins)."""


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sequence feature extraction
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

import re

SEQUON = re.compile(r"N[^P][ST]")


def count_sequons(seq: str) -> int:
    """N-X-S/T sequons, X != P, counted with overlap."""
    return sum(1 for i in range(len(seq) - 2) if SEQUON.match(seq, i))


def sequon_positions(seq: str) -> List[int]:
    return [i + 1 for i in range(len(seq) - 2) if SEQUON.match(seq, i)]


@dataclass
class ProteinSpec:
    """What the cost model needs to know about one protein."""
    name: str
    sequence: str                 # full precursor, signal peptide included
    signal_end: int = 0           # 1-based last residue of the signal peptide
    n_disulfide: int = 0
    n_sequon: Optional[int] = None        # default: computed from mature chain
    n_o_glyc_site: int = 0
    n_phosphosite: int = 0
    n_haem: int = 0
    accession: str = ""
    notes: str = ""

    @property
    def mature(self) -> str:
        return self.sequence[self.signal_end:]

    @property
    def signal(self) -> str:
        return self.sequence[:self.signal_end]

    def sequons(self) -> int:
        if self.n_sequon is not None:
            return self.n_sequon
        return count_sequons(self.mature)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cost computation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class CostResult:
    name: str
    length_precursor: int
    length_mature: int
    # the product
    product_formula: Dict[str, float]
    product_mass_da: float
    # per molecule
    aa_draw: Dict[str, float]            # residue letter -> count (net)
    atp: float
    gtp: float
    o2: float
    h2o2: float
    nadph: float
    gdpmann: float
    uacgam: float
    udpg: float
    dolmanp: float
    haem: float
    # derived
    carbon_in_product: float
    carbon_in_precursors: float
    atp_per_g: float = 0.0
    nadph_per_g: float = 0.0
    carbon_per_g: float = 0.0
    breakdown: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)


def compute_cost(spec: ProteinSpec, p: CostParams) -> CostResult:
    seq_full = spec.sequence
    seq_mat = spec.mature
    Lp, Lm = len(seq_full), len(seq_mat)

    # --- amino-acid draw --------------------------------------------------
    charged = seq_full if p.include_signal_peptide else seq_mat
    draw: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for a in charged:
        if a in AA_MET:
            draw[a] = draw.get(a, 0.0) + 1.0
    if p.include_signal_peptide and p.recycle_signal_peptide:
        for a in spec.signal:
            if a in AA_MET:
                draw[a] -= 1.0

    # --- product elemental formula (mature, modified chain) ---------------
    f: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for a in seq_mat:
        if a in AA_FORMULA:
            _add(f, AA_FORMULA[a])
    _add(f, H2O, -(Lm - 1))                 # peptide bonds
    n_ss = float(spec.n_disulfide)
    _add(f, {"H": -2.0 * n_ss})             # 2 H lost per disulfide
    n_seq = float(spec.sequons())
    _add(f, GLCNAC_RES, p.n_glycan_glcnac * n_seq)
    _add(f, MAN_RES, p.n_glycan_mannose * n_seq)
    _add(f, MAN_RES, p.o_mannose_per_site * spec.n_o_glyc_site)
    n_phos = float(spec.n_phosphosite) if p.phosphorylate else 0.0
    _add(f, HPO3, n_phos)
    n_haem = float(spec.n_haem) if spec.n_haem else p.haem_per_molecule
    _add(f, HAEM_B, n_haem)
    mass = formula_mass(f)

    # --- energy -----------------------------------------------------------
    atp_translation = p.atp_per_residue * Lp + p.initiation_atp
    atp_bip = p.bip_atp_per_residue * Lp
    atp_phos = p.atp_per_phosphorylation * n_phos
    atp = atp_translation + atp_bip + atp_phos
    gtp = p.transport_gtp_per_molecule

    # --- redox ------------------------------------------------------------
    o2 = p.o2_per_disulfide * n_ss
    h2o2 = o2
    nadph = p.isomerisation_cycles_per_disulfide * n_ss

    # --- glycan donors ----------------------------------------------------
    uacgam = p.n_glycan_glcnac * n_seq
    # core mannose up to Man5 comes straight from GDP-Man on the cytosolic
    # face; the rest is delivered as Dol-P-Man.
    core_direct = min(p.n_glycan_mannose, 5.0) * n_seq
    via_dolmanp = max(p.n_glycan_mannose - 5.0, 0.0) * n_seq \
        + p.o_mannose_per_site * spec.n_o_glyc_site
    gdpmann = core_direct + via_dolmanp     # Dol-P-Man itself is made from GDP-Man
    dolmanp = via_dolmanp
    udpg = p.n_glycan_transient_glucose * n_seq

    # --- carbon accounting -------------------------------------------------
    c_prod = f.get("C", 0.0)
    c_prec = sum(AA_FORMULA[a]["C"] * n for a, n in draw.items() if n > 0)
    c_prec += 6 * (gdpmann + udpg) + 8 * uacgam + 34 * n_haem

    r = CostResult(
        name=spec.name, length_precursor=Lp, length_mature=Lm,
        product_formula=f, product_mass_da=mass, aa_draw=draw,
        atp=atp, gtp=gtp, o2=o2, h2o2=h2o2, nadph=nadph,
        gdpmann=gdpmann, uacgam=uacgam, udpg=udpg, dolmanp=dolmanp,
        haem=n_haem, carbon_in_product=c_prod, carbon_in_precursors=c_prec,
    )
    g = mass / 1e3            # mmol-scale: 1 mmol protein = mass/1000 g
    r.atp_per_g = atp / g
    r.nadph_per_g = nadph / g
    r.carbon_per_g = c_prec / g
    r.breakdown = {
        "atp_translation": atp_translation,
        "atp_chaperone": atp_bip,
        "atp_phosphorylation": atp_phos,
        "gtp_transport": gtp,
        "o2_disulfide": o2,
        "nadph_isomerisation": nadph,
        "gdpmannose_glycan": gdpmann,
        "udpglcnac_glycan": uacgam,
        "udpglucose_transient": udpg,
        "haem": n_haem,
        "n_sequon": n_seq,
        "n_disulfide": n_ss,
        "n_phosphosite": n_phos,
    }
    return r


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GEM reaction construction
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_reactions(model, spec: ProteinSpec, p: CostParams,
                    rxn_prefix: str = "PROT_"):
    """Add synthesis + secretion reactions for `spec` to a cobra `model`.

    Returns (cost_result, synthesis_reaction, sink_reaction).
    The model is modified in place; wrap in `with model:` to undo.
    """
    import cobra

    r = compute_cost(spec, p)
    tag = rxn_prefix + spec.name

    prot_c = cobra.Metabolite(f"{tag}_c", name=f"{spec.name} (cytosol/secreted)",
                              compartment="c",
                              formula=formula_str(r.product_formula))

    stoich = {}

    def add(met_id, coeff):
        if coeff == 0:
            return
        m = model.metabolites.get_by_id(met_id)
        stoich[m] = stoich.get(m, 0.0) + coeff

    for a, n in r.aa_draw.items():
        add(AA_MET[a], -n)

    # translational and chaperone energy, as ATP equivalents
    add("atp_c", -r.atp)
    add("h2o_c", -r.atp)
    add("adp_c", r.atp)
    add("pi_c", r.atp)
    add("h_c", r.atp)

    # vesicular transport GTP
    add("gtp_c", -r.gtp)
    add("h2o_c", -r.gtp)
    add("gdp_c", r.gtp)
    add("pi_c", r.gtp)
    add("h_c", r.gtp)

    # water released by peptide-bond formation (mature chain)
    add("h2o_c", r.length_mature - 1)
    # water released when the signal peptide is hydrolysed off and recycled
    if p.include_signal_peptide and p.recycle_signal_peptide and spec.signal_end:
        add("h2o_c", -spec.signal_end)

    # oxidative folding
    add("o2_c", -r.o2)
    add("h2o2_c", r.h2o2)
    # futile isomerisation: NADPH -> NADP+ via glutathione reductase
    if r.nadph:
        add("nadph_c", -r.nadph)
        add("h_c", -r.nadph)
        add("nadp_c", r.nadph)
        # the electrons end up reducing O2 as well
        add("o2_c", -0.5 * r.nadph)
        add("h2o_c", r.nadph)

    # N- and O-glycan donors
    add("uacgam_c", -r.uacgam)
    add("udp_c", r.uacgam)
    add("gdpmann_c", -r.gdpmann)
    add("gdp_c", r.gdpmann)
    add("udpg_c", -r.udpg)
    add("udp_c", r.udpg)
    if p.recycle_transient_glucose and r.udpg:
        add("glc_D_c", r.udpg)

    # phosphorylation
    if r.breakdown["n_phosphosite"]:
        # ATP already charged above as ATP equivalents; the phosphoryl group
        # transferred to the protein must not also leave as free phosphate.
        add("pi_c", -r.breakdown["n_phosphosite"])

    # haem b
    if r.haem:
        if "pheme_c" not in model.metabolites:
            hm = model.metabolites.get_by_id("pheme_m")
            hc = cobra.Metabolite("pheme_c", name="Protoheme", compartment="c",
                                  formula=hm.formula)
            model.add_metabolites([hc])
            tr = cobra.Reaction("PHEMEtm", name="Protoheme mitochondrial export")
            tr.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
            tr.add_metabolites({hm: -1.0, hc: 1.0})
            model.add_reactions([tr])
        add("pheme_c", -r.haem)

    stoich[prot_c] = stoich.get(prot_c, 0.0) + 1.0

    rxn = cobra.Reaction(tag, name=f"{spec.name} synthesis and secretion")
    rxn.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
    model.add_reactions([rxn])
    rxn.add_metabolites(stoich)

    sink = cobra.Reaction("EX_" + tag, name=f"{spec.name} secretion (exchange)")
    sink.bounds = (0.0, 1000.0)
    model.add_reactions([sink])
    sink.add_metabolites({prot_c: -1.0})

    return r, rxn, sink


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loading the target panel
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def specs_from_uniprot_json(path: str,
                            phospho_from_annotation: bool = True
                            ) -> Dict[str, ProteinSpec]:
    with open(path) as fh:
        recs = json.load(fh)
    out = {}
    for name, d in recs.items():
        sp_end = d["signal"][0]["end"] if d["signal"] else 0
        n_ss = len(d["disulfide"])
        phos = 0
        o_gly = 0
        n_gly_ann = 0
        for m in d["mod_res"]:
            if "Phospho" in (m["desc"] or ""):
                phos += 1
        for c in d["carbohyd"]:
            desc = (c["desc"] or "")
            if desc.startswith("N-linked"):
                n_gly_ann += 1
            elif desc.startswith("O-linked"):
                o_gly += 1
        haem = 1 if ("globin" in name or "hemoglobin" in name) else 0
        out[name] = ProteinSpec(
            name=name, sequence=d["sequence"], signal_end=sp_end,
            n_disulfide=n_ss, n_o_glyc_site=o_gly,
            n_phosphosite=phos if phospho_from_annotation else 0,
            n_haem=haem, accession=d["accession"],
            notes=f"uniprot_Nglyc_annotated={n_gly_ann}",
        )
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    specs = specs_from_uniprot_json(
        os.path.join(here, "..", "data", "sequences", "targets.json"))
    p = CostParams()
    print(f"{'protein':38s} {'Lmat':>5s} {'SS':>3s} {'Nseq':>4s} {'P':>3s} "
          f"{'kDa':>7s} {'ATP/mol':>8s} {'ATP/g':>8s} {'C/g':>7s}")
    for n, s in sorted(specs.items()):
        r = compute_cost(s, p)
        print(f"{n:38s} {r.length_mature:5d} {int(s.n_disulfide):3d} "
              f"{int(s.sequons()):4d} {int(s.n_phosphosite):3d} "
              f"{r.product_mass_da/1000:7.2f} {r.atp:8.0f} "
              f"{r.atp_per_g:8.1f} {r.carbon_per_g:7.1f}")
