content.content:
paper/01_front_matter.md:25:Two candidate positive findings arose during this work and neither survived audit, which is reported rather than concealed. The second is documented at length in Appendix F because of what it demonstrates: a correlation between mean predicted disorder and ceiling utilisation, reported at ρ = −0.833 with a permutation p of 0.00025, FDR control across 32 features and a leave-one-out check that held throughout, fell to ρ = −0.483, p = 0.117 once three faults in the underlying titre records were corrected — an intracellular yield recorded as a secretion titre, a best-titre join that pooled orthologues so that one protein borrowed another species' number, and a carrier construct counted as its passenger. **Four statistical controls that are normally treated as sufficient all passed on data that did not mean what its column headings said.** The direction of the disorder effect is consistent across every fit and the thesis treats it as an untested hypothesis, naming the measurement that would decide it: titres for α-S1-, α-S2- and β-casein, the three most disordered proteins in the target class and the three with no published number in any microbial host.
paper/01_front_matter.md:59:I am grateful to my supervisor for the latitude to let this project change shape twice: once when the prior-art audit removed the object it had been built to produce, and again when a corrected database removed a finding that had already been written up. Both reversals improved the thesis, and neither would have survived a less patient review.
paper/02_introduction.md:55:Honesty about novelty is more useful than enthusiasm about it, and the prior-art audit conducted for this thesis (Chapter 2) found a great deal of relevant prior work.
paper/02_introduction.md:65:3. **Each published titre expressed as a fraction of its own protein's ceiling**, which converts the field's incommensurable numbers into one comparable quantity, and the attribution of the residual — including the negative results, which turn out to be the informative ones, and two candidate positive findings that were withdrawn under audit rather than published.
paper/02_introduction.md:71:Chapter 2 reviews the field and reports the prior-art audit in full, including the work that comes closest to this one and exactly how close it comes. Chapter 3 sets out the computational methods, the data provenance rules and the verification procedures, including the independent reimplementation that cross-checked the central numbers. Chapter 4 computes the stoichiometric ceilings and decomposes the post-translational load. Chapter 5 presents the ceiling–gap measurement. Chapter 6 tests what the gap tracks and reports both the positive and the negative findings. Chapter 7 derives protein-specific metabolic engineering targets. Chapter 8 develops the techno-economic consequences. Chapter 9 discusses limitations, the confounds that the analysis cannot remove, and the minimal wet-laboratory programme that would test the predictions made here.
paper/03_literature_review.md:5:The chapter has three jobs. The first is the ordinary one of a literature review: to establish what is known, with sources. The second is to extract from each literature the specific quantities this thesis later uses or tests, and to say where those quantities came from. The third, set out in §2.8, is to establish by systematic search which parts of the proposed contribution have already been made by someone else, because a novelty claim that has not been audited is not a claim but a hope.
paper/03_literature_review.md:7:**The corpus this chapter reads.** The literature corpus assembled for this thesis contains 230 references across nine topic clusters. Every identifier was resolved against Crossref and confirmed independently at doi.org: 189 of the 230 carry a verified DOI, the remaining 41 have none and the reason is stated for each, and none was inferred. That pass was treated as blocking rather than cosmetic, because an earlier audit found that inferred identifiers were wrong roughly half the time — and an inferred DOI looks exactly like a resolved one and fails silently. Resolution corrected 11 first authors and 12 years that would otherwise have become wrong in-text citations, recovered 48 identifiers that an initial automated pass had missed, and exposed two papers the bibliography had listed twice. Counts by cluster: industry and regulation 21; *Komagataella phaffii* as a host 34; *Trichoderma reesei* as a host 17; milk proteins 31; egg and haem proteins 16; computational methods 49; genome-scale modelling and protein cost 28; techno-economics and life-cycle assessment 17; prior art on producibility prediction 17.
paper/03_literature_review.md:71:This is the mechanism that remains the leading candidate for the residual gap of Chapter 5, and it is important to be exact about the evidential status this thesis can claim for it. The candidate is strong because the host literature responds to it: interventions aimed at folding and secretion capacity raise titres repeatedly and across unrelated products. But §6.2.1 records why *this* thesis cannot claim to have measured it. An association between disulfide density and ceiling utilisation, which appeared to support the folding hypothesis directly, did not survive annotation-grade measurement of disulfide counts, and it was withdrawn. The positive evidence for folding in this thesis is therefore the mechanism reported in the primary sources, not anything this analysis measured — a distinction §6.7 states again rather than allowing to blur.
paper/03_literature_review.md:169:The published route to high titre is precisely that. High-level secretory production of leghemoglobin in *P. pastoris* was achieved through enhanced globin expression combined with remodelling of haem biosynthesis (Shao et al. 2022, 10.1016/j.biortech.2022.127884), and the same logic — balanced globin expression and haem biosynthesis — had earlier been established for human haemoglobin in *S. cerevisiae* (Liu et al. 2014, 10.1016/j.ymben.2013.10.010). Haemoglobin yield in yeast has also been improved by engineering its degradation rather than its synthesis (Ishchuk et al. 2021, 10.1016/j.ymben.2021.05.002), which is a reminder that for a cofactor-binding protein, stability of the holoprotein and supply of the cofactor are separate problems. High-level leghemoglobin expression has been achieved in *Kluyveromyces marxianus* by remodelling haem metabolism (Tian et al. 2024, 10.3389/fbioe.2023.1329016), and metabolic engineering of *S. cerevisiae* for haem itself establishes the pathway as an engineering target in its own right (Lee et al. 2024, 10.1002/biot.202400351). Growth-coupled haem biosynthesis in *P. pastoris* has been analysed with metabolic modelling (Pentjuss et al. 2023, 10.1038/s41598-023-42865-w), which is the closest prior art to the leghemoglobin part of Chapter 4. Production and purification from different expression media is documented by Bolmanis and colleagues (2023, 10.3390/pr11113215), and the protein's structure, production, safety and food applications are reviewed by Ahmad and colleagues (2023, 10.1016/j.tifs.2023.104199).
paper/03_literature_review.md:189:This thesis computes disorder with metapredict (version 3.1.01), on the mature chain after signal-peptide removal, and retains the dependency-free charge–hydropathy FoldIndex as a transparent fallback. The choice of statistic turned out to matter more than the choice of predictor, and §6.5 records why: the pre-specified statistic was the *fraction* of residues above a disorder threshold, which is identically zero for every globular protein in the panel and therefore discards the gradient among them, whereas the *mean* disorder score retains it. The two statistics give very different correlations with ceiling utilisation, and the episode is reported as a methodological error of this thesis rather than a feature of the data.
paper/03_literature_review.md:237:Two papers compute per-protein costs in a model and are the direct prior art for Chapter 4. Feizi and colleagues modelled the protein secretory machinery in *S. cerevisiae* at genome scale and computed per-protein costs in ATP, GTP, GDP-mannose and UDP-GlcNAc across the proteome (2013, 10.1371/journal.pone.0063284). Gutierrez and colleagues reconstructed the mammalian secretory pathway and computed per-protein metabolic costs and limits of secretion, together with the features most affecting it (2020, 10.1038/s41467-019-13867-y). The supply-chain framing of protein production and secretion in yeasts and mammalian cells (Klein et al. 2015, 10.1007/s10295-014-1569-2) is the conceptual bridge between the cost literature and the host-engineering literature.
paper/03_literature_review.md:267:This thesis was preceded by a systematic prior-art audit of roughly 220 screened records with verified identifiers. The audit's full detail, including the searches run and the records screened, is in **Appendix G**; what belongs in the body of the chapter is the concession, and it is short.
paper/03_literature_review.md:271:**Protein-specific secretion reactions with bottleneck attribution are established work.** pcSecYeast (Li et al. 2022) builds protein-specific secretion reactions from sequence and post-translational requirements for eight recombinant proteins, including a haemoglobin, and makes explicit per-protein bottleneck calls. This is the closest methodological prior art to Chapter 6, and it is cited as the method's origin rather than competed with.
paper/03_literature_review.md:273:**Predicting producibility from sequence is a developed field, including in fungi.** Presep (Tian et al. 2013) predicts secretion propensity specifically in *P. pastoris*; the phrase "predicting protein producibility" was used for filamentous fungi in 2017 (Dykstra, Rousu and Arvas, 10.1101/138560); and large-scale empirical analyses populate the space thoroughly — 11,430 production experiments (Bhandari et al. 2021), determinants across the human secretome (Masson et al. 2025), deep protein representations for expression prediction (Martiny et al. 2021), ExpressUrself (Dunne et al. 2022), PERISCOPE-Opt (Packiam et al. 2022) and high-throughput developability assays at library scale (Golinski et al. 2021) — while the biologics developability-index tradition (Lauer et al. 2012) establishes composite sequence-based scores as a legitimate construct. **A "producibility index" is therefore not a novel object, and this thesis does not claim one.** An earlier framing did; the audit retired it, and §6.4 and §5.2.2 supply the quantitative reason it could not have worked on this data anyway.

This is the mechanism that remains the leading candidate for the residual gap of Chapter 5, and it is important to be exact about the evidential status this thesis can claim for it. The candidate is strong because the host literature responds to it: interventions aimed at folding and secretion capacity raise titres repeatedly and across unrelated products. But §6.2.1 records why *this* thesis cannot claim to have measured it. An association between disulfide density and ceiling utilisation, which appeared to support the folding hypothesis directly, did not survive annotation-grade measurement of disulfide counts, and it was withdrawn. The positive evidence for folding in this thesis is therefore the mechanism reported in the primary sources, not anything this analysis measured — a distinction §6.7 states again rather than allowing to blur.
===
This thesis computes disorder with metapredict (version 3.1.01), on the mature chain after signal-peptide removal, and retains the dependency-free charge–hydropathy FoldIndex as a transparent fallback. The choice of statistic turned out to matter more than the choice of predictor, and §6.5 records why: the pre-specified statistic was the *fraction* of residues above a disorder threshold, which is identically zero for every globular protein in the panel and therefore discards the gradient among them, whereas the *mean* disorder score retains it. The two statistics give very different correlations with ceiling utilisation, and the episode is reported as a methodological error of this thesis rather than a feature of the data.
===
§2.8 states the concession. This appendix records the audit that produced it, because a novelty claim rests on the thoroughness of the search that failed to find a competitor, and that search should be inspectable.

### G.1 What was searched

The audit screened roughly 220 records with verified identifiers, assembled from four kinds of query run against Europe PMC, Crossref and general web search:

1. **Method queries** — combinations of {genome-scale, constraint-based, flux balance, proteome-constrained} with {protein cost, secretion cost, per-protein yield, maximum theoretical yield} and with {*Pichia pastoris*, *Komagataella phaffii*, *Trichoderma reesei*, yeast, CHO}.
2. **Object queries** — combinations of {producibility, expressibility, secretability, developability, expression prediction} with {index, score, predictor, sequence-based}.

content.content:
## Repository map

| Path | What is in it |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Every analysis script. See `src/README.md` for the run order. |
| `docs/` | The prior-art audit, every cost parameter with its source, the titer-database schema, and the original brief. |
| `data/literature/` | The curated titer corpus (306 records) and the 232-entry bibliography, with their verification reports. |
| `data/sequences/` | The curated 20-protein panel and the harvested sequences. |
| `data/external/` | UniProt entries, AlphaFold models, *K. phaffii* CDS. |
| `data/models/` | The genome-scale metabolic models, iMT1026v3 among them. |
| `results/tables/` | Every output table and results write-up. |
| `paper/` | The manuscript. |

## Reading order for the results

1. `results/tables/variance_decomposition.md` — the headline, with bootstrap
   intervals and the variance components.
2. `results/tables/ceiling_gap.csv` — ceiling, best measured titer and
   utilisation, per protein and host.
3. `results/tables/food_subset_signal.md` — the sequence-feature search, and a
   **retraction**: an earlier disorder correlation of ρ −0.833 did not survive
   correct titer matching and is recorded here with the reason it looked robust.
4. `results/tables/product_classes_and_filters.md` — filter sensitivity.
5. `data/literature/titers_merged_report.md` — how the corpus was built.

====
| `adopt_doi_candidates.py` | Checks each suggested DOI on title, year, author and work type before adopting it, then confirms it resolves at doi.org independently of Crossref. |

## Stage 4 — model

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `protein_cost.py` | The cost engine: a mass- and electron-balanced synthesis and secretion reaction per protein. Every tunable parameter lives in `CostParams` and each is documented with a source in `docs/COST_PARAMETERS.md`. Reactions are closed on protons generically, with an assertion that nothing but hydrogen may remain unbalanced. |
| `yields.py` | Maximum theoretical yield in grams of protein per gram of substrate, on glycerol, methanol, both, or glucose. |
| `features.py` | The sequence-feature panel: FoldIndex, charge patterning κ, GRAVY, host amino-acid divergence, biosynthetic cost, and metapredict disorder when it is installed. Every feature is computed from the **mature** chain. |
| `ceilings_by_accession.py` | Ceilings for all 36 held accessions rather than only the curated panel, so therapeutics and collagens have ceilings to compare against. |

## Stage 5 — analyse

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ceiling_gap.py` | The per-protein table: ceiling, best defensible measured titer, and utilisation. Titers are matched on **both** canonical name and source organism, and only secreted measurements are used; the comment above `CORPUS_LABEL` records the three faults that made both rules necessary. |
| `gap_attribution.py` | Univariate Spearman correlations of each feature against the gap, with bootstrap intervals, permutation p-values and Benjamini–Hochberg correction. No multi-feature model is fitted; at this sample size reporting one would be indefensible. |
| `food_subset_signal.py` | The same search restricted to food proteins, with the two-cluster diagnostic that leave-one-out cannot provide. Contains the retraction of the earlier disorder result. |
| `variance_decomposition.py` | The headline. Splits the variance in realised production into between-protein, between-study and within-study components using crossed random intercepts, and reports the distributional statistics with bootstrap intervals. |

## If you only run three

    python3 src/uniprot_features.py      # self-test; must pass before anything else
    python3 src/ceiling_gap.py           # the per-protein ceiling table
    python3 src/variance_decomposition.py # the headline result

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy this session's working transcripts into the repository, redacted.

The repository is meant to be self-contained: the analysis, the sources it
rests on, and the record of how it was produced. The last of those is the
session transcripts, which are written by the agent harness outside the
repository and are lost when the container is reclaimed.

They cannot be committed as they stand. A transcript contains the email
address of the account that ran the session, the member's display name, links
that carry a session identifier, and, in principle, any credential that passed
through a shell command. This script copies them with those removed, and
refuses to write anything if the check at the end still finds one.

What is redacted:

* every email address except `noreply@anthropic.com`, which is a placeholder
  and identifies nobody;
* the display name of the person the session worked for, passed as --name;
* claude.ai session links, which identify an account's session;
* anything shaped like an API token (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, a bearer header).

What is deliberately kept: the repository's own name and branches, file paths
inside the container, every command run and its output, and the full text of
the reasoning. Those are the record.

Usage:
    python3 src/record_history.py --name "<display name>"
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "history"
SOURCES = [
    Path("/root/.claude/projects"),
]

KEEP_EMAILS = {"noreply@anthropic.com"}

EMAIL = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")
SESSION_LINK = re.compile(r"https://claude\.ai/code/session_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+")
SESSION_ID = re.compile(r"\bsession_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b")
TOKENS = [
    re.compile(r"\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"),
    re.compile(r"(?i)\b(?:authorization|bearer)\b[:=\s]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}"),
]


def redact(text: str, names: list[str]) -> str:
    def email_sub(m: re.Match) -> str:
        return m.group(0) if m.group(0).lower() in KEEP_EMAILS else "[email redacted]"

    text = EMAIL.sub(email_sub, text)
    text = SESSION_LINK.sub("[session link redacted]", text)
    text = SESSION_ID.sub("session_[redacted]", text)
    for pat in TOKENS:
        text = pat.sub("[credential redacted]", text)
    for name in names:
        if not name:
            continue
        text = re.sub(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}\b", "[name redacted]", text,
                      flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return text


def residue(text: str, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Anything the redaction should have removed and did not."""
    found = []
    for m in EMAIL.finditer(text):
        if m.group(0).lower() not in KEEP_EMAILS:
            found.append(m.group(0))
    for pat in (SESSION_LINK, SESSION_ID, *TOKENS):
        found += [m.group(0) for m in pat.finditer(text)]
    for name in names:
        if name and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}\b", text, re.I):
            found.append(name)
    return found


def copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path, names: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    files = kept = 0
    for path in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        files += 1
        rel = path.relative_to(src)
        target = dst / rel
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        clean = redact(text, names)
        left = residue(clean, names)
        if left:
            print(f"  REFUSED {rel}: {sorted(set(left))[:3]}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        target.write_text(clean)
        kept += 1
    return files, kept


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--name", action="append", default=[],
                    help="a display name to redact; repeatable")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if OUT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT / "transcripts", ignore_errors=True)
    (OUT / "transcripts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    total = kept = 0
    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            print(f"  {src} not present in this container; skipped")
            continue
        f, k = copy_tree(src, OUT / "transcripts", args.name)
        total += f
        kept += k

    index = ["# Session transcripts", "",
             "The raw working record of the sessions that produced this",
             "repository, copied out of the agent harness and redacted by",
             "`src/record_history.py`. Email addresses, the member's display",
             "name, session links and anything shaped like a credential are",
             "removed; commands, outputs, reasoning and file paths are kept.",
             "",
             "Each session that ran in its own container keeps its own",
             "transcript there, so only the sessions whose container this is",
             "appear below.",
             "", "| File | Size | SHA-256 (first 16) |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for path in sorted((OUT / "transcripts").rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            rel = path.relative_to(OUT / "transcripts")
            index.append(f"| `{rel}` | {path.stat().st_size // 1024} KB "
                         f"| `{digest(path)}` |")
    (OUT / "transcripts" / "README.md").write_text("\n".join(index) + "\n")

    print(f"copied {kept} of {total} transcript files -> {OUT / 'transcripts'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"),
    re.compile(r"(?i)\b(?:authorization|bearer)\b[:=\s]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}"),
]


def redact(text: str, names: list[str]) -> str:
    def email_sub(m: re.Match) -> str:
        return m.group(0) if m.group(0).lower() in KEEP_EMAILS else "[email redacted]"

    text = EMAIL.sub(email_sub, text)
    text = SESSION_LINK.sub("[session link redacted]", text)
    text = SESSION_ID.sub("session_[redacted]", text)
    for pat in TOKENS:
        text = pat.sub("[credential redacted]", text)
    for name in names:
        if not name:
            continue
        text = re.sub(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}\b", "[name redacted]", text,
                      flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return text


def residue(text: str, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Anything the redaction should have removed and did not."""
    found = []
    for m in EMAIL.finditer(text):
        if m.group(0).lower() not in KEEP_EMAILS:
            found.append(m.group(0))
    for pat in (SESSION_LINK, SESSION_ID, *TOKENS):
        found += [m.group(0) for m in pat.finditer(text)]
    for name in names:
        if name and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}\b", text, re.I):
            found.append(name)
    return found


def copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path, names: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    files = kept = 0
    for path in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        files += 1
        rel = path.relative_to(src)
        target = dst / rel
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        clean = redact(text, names)
        left = residue(clean, names)
        if left:
            print(f"  REFUSED {rel}: {sorted(set(left))[:3]}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        target.write_text(clean)
        kept += 1
    return files, kept


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()[:16]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--name", action="append", default=[],
                    help="a display name to redact; repeatable")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if OUT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT / "transcripts", ignore_errors=True)
    (OUT / "transcripts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    total = kept = 0
    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            print(f"  {src} not present in this container; skipped")
            continue
        f, k = copy_tree(src, OUT / "transcripts", args.name)
        total += f
        kept += k

    index = ["# Session transcripts", "",
             "The raw working record of the sessions that produced this",
             "repository, copied out of the agent harness and redacted by",
             "`src/record_history.py`. Email addresses, the member's display",
             "name, session links and anything shaped like a credential are",
             "removed; commands, outputs, reasoning and file paths are kept.",
             "",
             "Each session that ran in its own container keeps its own",
             "transcript there, so only the sessions whose container this is",
             "appear below.",
             "", "| File | Size | SHA-256 (first 16) |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for path in sorted((OUT / "transcripts").rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            rel = path.relative_to(OUT / "transcripts")
            index.append(f"| `{rel}` | {path.stat().st_size // 1024} KB "
                         f"| `{digest(path)}` |")
    (OUT / "transcripts" / "README.md").write_text("\n".join(index) + "\n")

    print(f"copied {kept} of {total} transcript files -> {OUT / 'transcripts'}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pull every source the thesis cites into the repository, where that is allowed.

A bibliography is a set of promises that someone else's server will still be
there. This turns as much of it as licensing permits into files in the
repository, and records, for every entry, either where the local copy is or why
there is not one.

The rules, which are about redistribution rather than access:

* **Open-access full text from Europe PMC.** Europe PMC states an entry's open
  access status and licence. Where it reports open access and a PMCID, the
  full text XML is fetched and saved. Those are author-retained CC licences
  that permit redistribution with attribution, which the manifest records.
* **US government documents.** FDA letters, GRAS notices and Federal Register
  items are works of the US government and are not under copyright. Their PDFs
  are fetched directly.
* **Everything else gets metadata and a link.** A paywalled paper, a trade
  press article or a company page may be read at its source but not
  redistributed here. The manifest carries the DOI, the URL, the resolved
  metadata and the reason no copy is stored, which is what makes the citation
  checkable without infringing anything.

Nothing here sends identifying information to any service: requests carry a
generic client name and no contact address.

Outputs:
    data/sources/fulltext/*.xml      open-access full texts
    data/sources/documents/*.pdf     public-domain government documents
    data/sources/metadata/*.json     resolved metadata for every entry
    data/sources/manifest.tsv        one row per entry, machine readable
    data/sources/MANIFEST.md         the same, readable, with the counts

Usage:
    python3 src/fetch_sources.py            # resume; skips what is present
    python3 src/fetch_sources.py --refresh  # re-fetch metadata
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
BIB = ROOT / "data" / "literature" / "bibliography.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "sources"
FULLTEXT = OUT / "fulltext"
DOCUMENTS = OUT / "documents"
METADATA = OUT / "metadata"

EPMC = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest"
UA = "ashry-thesis-archive/1.0 (research archive; no contact stored)"
PAUSE = 0.34                      # about three requests a second

# Domains whose documents are works of the US federal government, and so are
# not under copyright and may be stored here.
PUBLIC_DOMAIN = (
    "fda.gov", "govinfo.gov", "federalregister.gov", "ncbi.nlm.nih.gov",
    "nih.gov", "usda.gov", "hfpappexternal.fda.gov",
)


def get(url: str, timeout: int = 45) -> bytes | None:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as fh:
            return fh.read()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, urllib.error.HTTPError, TimeoutError, OSError):
        return None
    finally:
        time.sleep(PAUSE)


def key_for(row: dict, n: int) -> str:
    author = (row.get("authors") or "anon").split(",")[0].split(" ")[0]
    author = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z]", "", author).lower() or "anon"
    year = re.sub(r"[^0-9]", "", str(row.get("year") or ""))[:4] or "nd"
    return f"{n:03d}_{author}_{year}"


def europepmc(doi: str, title: str) -> dict | None:
    """Resolve an entry at Europe PMC, by DOI if there is one, else by title."""
    if doi:
        q = f'DOI:"{doi}"'
    elif title:
        q = 'TITLE:"%s"' % title.replace('"', "")
    else:
        return None
    url = (f"{EPMC}/search?query={urllib.parse.quote(q)}"
           "&resultType=core&format=json&pageSize=1")
    raw = get(url)
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        hits = json.loads(raw)["resultList"]["result"]
    except (ValueError, KeyError):
        return None
    return hits[0] if hits else None


def redistributable(rec: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Whether Europe PMC says this full text may be stored, and the reason."""
    if not rec:
        return False, "no Europe PMC record"
    if (rec.get("isOpenAccess") or "N").upper() != "Y":
        return False, "not open access"
    if not rec.get("pmcid"):
        return False, "open access but no PMC full text"
    licence = (rec.get("license") or "").lower()
    if licence and not licence.startswith(("cc", "pd", "publ")):
        return False, f"licence {licence} does not permit redistribution"
    return True, licence or "open access, licence unstated"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    for d in (FULLTEXT, DOCUMENTS, METADATA):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    rows = list(csv.DictReader(BIB.open()))
    if args.limit:
        rows = rows[: args.limit]

    manifest = []
    counts = {"fulltext": 0, "document": 0, "metadata": 0, "unresolved": 0}

    for n, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
        key = key_for(row, n)
        doi = (row.get("doi") or "").strip()
        url = (row.get("url") or "").strip()
        title = (row.get("title") or "").strip()
        meta_path = METADATA / f"{key}.json"

        if meta_path.exists() and not args.refresh:
            record = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        else:
            rec = europepmc(doi, title)
            record = {
                "key": key, "cluster": row.get("cluster"),
                "authors": row.get("authors"), "year": row.get("year"),
                "title": title, "venue": row.get("venue"),
                "type": row.get("type"), "doi": doi, "url": url,
                "europepmc": {k: rec.get(k) for k in
                              ("id", "source", "pmid", "pmcid", "doi",
                               "isOpenAccess", "license", "firstPublicationDate",
                               "journalInfo", "citedByCount")} if rec else None,
            }
            meta_path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")

        rec = record.get("europepmc")
        stored, reason = "", ""

        ok, why = redistributable(rec or {})
        ft = FULLTEXT / f"{key}.xml"
        if ok and not ft.exists():
            body = get(f"{EPMC}/{rec['pmcid']}/fullTextXML")
            if body and b"<article" in body[:4000]:
                ft.write_bytes(body)
            else:
                why = "open access but full text not served"
        if ft.exists():
            stored = str(ft.relative_to(ROOT))
            reason = f"open access ({rec.get('license') or 'licence unstated'})"
            counts["fulltext"] += 1

        if not stored and url and any(d in url for d in PUBLIC_DOMAIN):
            pdf = DOCUMENTS / f"{key}.pdf"
            if not pdf.exists():
                body = get(url)
                if body and body[:5] == b"%PDF-":
                    pdf.write_bytes(body)
            if pdf.exists():
                stored = str(pdf.relative_to(ROOT))
                reason = "work of the US government, not under copyright"
                counts["document"] += 1

        if not stored:
            reason = why if rec else (
                "no record at Europe PMC; metadata and link only")
            counts["metadata" if rec else "unresolved"] += 1

        manifest.append({
            "key": key,
            "cluster": row.get("cluster"),
            "authors": row.get("authors"),
            "year": row.get("year"),
            "title": title,
            "venue": row.get("venue"),
            "doi": doi,
            "url": url,
            "pmcid": (rec or {}).get("pmcid") or "",
            "local_copy": stored,
            "why": reason,
            "metadata": str(meta_path.relative_to(ROOT)),
        })
        if n % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  {n}/{len(rows)}", file=sys.stderr)

    fields = list(manifest[0].keys())
    with (OUT / "manifest.tsv").open("w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields, delimiter="\t")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(manifest)

    lines = [
        "# Source manifest", "",
        f"Every one of the {len(manifest)} bibliography entries, with the local "
        "copy where one may be stored and the reason where one may not.",
        "Generated by `src/fetch_sources.py`.", "",
        f"* Open-access full texts stored: **{counts['fulltext']}**",
        f"* Public-domain government documents stored: **{counts['document']}**",
        f"* Metadata and link only: **{counts['metadata'] + counts['unresolved']}**",
        "",
        "A missing copy is a licensing limit, not a gap in the record: the DOI, "
        "the URL and the resolved metadata are here for every entry, in "
        "`data/sources/metadata/`.", "",
        "| # | Entry | Identifier | Local copy | Why |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for row in manifest:
        ident = row["doi"] or row["url"] or "—"
        if len(ident) > 60:
            ident = ident[:57] + "…"
        who = (row["authors"] or "").split(",")[0]
        lines.append(
            f"| {row['key'].split('_')[0]} | {who} {row['year'] or ''} — "
            f"{row['title'][:70]} | `{ident}` | "
            f"{('`' + row['local_copy'] + '`') if row['local_copy'] else '—'} "
            f"| {row['why']} |")
    (OUT / "MANIFEST.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

    print(json.dumps(counts, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pull every source the thesis cites into the repository, where that is allowed.

A bibliography is a set of promises that someone else's server will still be
there. This turns as much of it as licensing permits into files in the
repository, and records, for every entry, either where the local copy is or why
there is not one.

The rules, which are about redistribution rather than access:

* **Open-access full text from Europe PMC.** Europe PMC states an entry's open
  access status and licence. Where it reports open access and a PMCID, the
  full text XML is fetched and saved. Those are author-retained CC licences
  that permit redistribution with attribution, which the manifest records.
* **US government documents.** FDA letters, GRAS notices and Federal Register
  items are works of the US government and are not under copyright. Their PDFs
  are fetched directly.
* **Everything else gets metadata and a link.** A paywalled paper, a trade
  press article or a company page may be read at its source but not
  redistributed here. The manifest carries the DOI, the URL, the resolved
  metadata and the reason no copy is stored, which is what makes the citation
  checkable without infringing anything.

Nothing here sends identifying information to any service: requests carry a
generic client name and no contact address.

Outputs:
    data/sources/fulltext/*.xml      open-access full texts
    data/sources/documents/*.pdf     public-domain government documents
    data/sources/metadata/*.json     resolved metadata for every entry
    data/sources/manifest.tsv        one row per entry, machine readable
    data/sources/MANIFEST.md         the same, readable, with the counts

Usage:
    python3 src/fetch_sources.py            # resume; skips what is present
    python3 src/fetch_sources.py --refresh  # re-fetch metadata
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
BIB = ROOT / "data" / "literature" / "bibliography.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "sources"
FULLTEXT = OUT / "fulltext"
DOCUMENTS = OUT / "documents"
METADATA = OUT / "metadata"

EPMC = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest"
UA = "ashry-thesis-archive/1.0 (research archive; no contact stored)"
PAUSE = 0.34                      # about three requests a second

# Domains whose documents are works of the US federal government, and so are
# not under copyright and may be stored here.
PUBLIC_DOMAIN = (
    "fda.gov", "govinfo.gov", "federalregister.gov", "ncbi.nlm.nih.gov",
    "nih.gov", "usda.gov", "hfpappexternal.fda.gov",
)


def get(url: str, timeout: int = 45) -> bytes | None:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as fh:
            return fh.read()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, urllib.error.HTTPError, TimeoutError, OSError):
        return None
    finally:
        time.sleep(PAUSE)


def key_for(row: dict, n: int) -> str:
    author = (row.get("authors") or "anon").split(",")[0].split(" ")[0]
    author = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z]", "", author).lower() or "anon"
    year = re.sub(r"[^0-9]", "", str(row.get("year") or ""))[:4] or "nd"
    return f"{n:03d}_{author}_{year}"


def europepmc(doi: str, title: str) -> dict | None:
    """Resolve an entry at Europe PMC, by DOI if there is one, else by title."""
    if doi:
        q = f'DOI:"{doi}"'
    elif title:
        q = 'TITLE:"%s"' % title.replace('"', "")
    else:
        return None
    url = (f"{EPMC}/search?query={urllib.parse.quote(q)}"
           "&resultType=core&format=json&pageSize=1")
    raw = get(url)
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        hits = json.loads(raw)["resultList"]["result"]
    except (ValueError, KeyError):
        return None
    return hits[0] if hits else None


def redistributable(rec: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Whether Europe PMC says this full text may be stored, and the reason."""
    if not rec:
        return False, "no Europe PMC record"
    if (rec.get("isOpenAccess") or "N").upper() != "Y":
        return False, "not open access"
    if not rec.get("pmcid"):
        return False, "open access but no PMC full text"
    licence = (rec.get("license") or "").lower()
    if licence and not licence.startswith(("cc", "pd", "publ")):
        return False, f"licence {licence} does not permit redistribution"
    return True, licence or "open access, licence unstated"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    for d in (FULLTEXT, DOCUMENTS, METADATA):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    rows = list(csv.DictReader(BIB.open()))
    if args.limit:
        rows = rows[: args.limit]

    manifest = []
    counts = {"fulltext": 0, "document": 0, "metadata": 0, "unresolved": 0}

    for n, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
        key = key_for(row, n)
        doi = (row.get("doi") or "").strip()
        url = (row.get("url") or "").strip()
        title = (row.get("title") or "").strip()
        meta_path = METADATA / f"{key}.json"

        if meta_path.exists() and not args.refresh:
            record = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        else:
            rec = europepmc(doi, title)
            record = {
                "key": key, "cluster": row.get("cluster"),
                "authors": row.get("authors"), "year": row.get("year"),
                "title": title, "venue": row.get("venue"),
                "type": row.get("type"), "doi": doi, "url": url,
                "europepmc": {k: rec.get(k) for k in
                              ("id", "source", "pmid", "pmcid", "doi",
                               "isOpenAccess", "license", "firstPublicationDate",
                               "journalInfo", "citedByCount")} if rec else None,
            }
            meta_path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")

        rec = record.get("europepmc")
        stored, reason = "", ""

        ok, why = redistributable(rec or {})
        ft = FULLTEXT / f"{key}.xml"
        if ok and not ft.exists():
            body = get(f"{EPMC}/{rec['pmcid']}/fullTextXML")
            if body and b"<article" in body[:4000]:
                ft.write_bytes(body)
            else:
                why = "open access but full text not served"
        if ft.exists():
            stored = str(ft.relative_to(ROOT))
            reason = f"open access ({rec.get('license') or 'licence unstated'})"
            counts["fulltext"] += 1

        if not stored and url and any(d in url for d in PUBLIC_DOMAIN):
            pdf = DOCUMENTS / f"{key}.pdf"
            if not pdf.exists():
                body = get(url)
                if body and body[:5] == b"%PDF-":
                    pdf.write_bytes(body)
            if pdf.exists():
                stored = str(pdf.relative_to(ROOT))
                reason = "work of the US government, not under copyright"
                counts["document"] += 1

        if not stored:
            reason = why if rec else (
                "no record at Europe PMC; metadata and link only")
            counts["metadata" if rec else "unresolved"] += 1

        manifest.append({
            "key": key,
            "cluster": row.get("cluster"),
            "authors": row.get("authors"),
            "year": row.get("year"),
            "title": title,
            "venue": row.get("venue"),
            "doi": doi,
            "url": url,
            "pmcid": (rec or {}).get("pmcid") or "",
            "local_copy": stored,
            "why": reason,
            "metadata": str(meta_path.relative_to(ROOT)),
        })
        if n % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  {n}/{len(rows)}", file=sys.stderr)

    fields = list(manifest[0].keys())
    with (OUT / "manifest.tsv").open("w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields, delimiter="\t")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(manifest)

    lines = [
        "# Source manifest", "",
        f"Every one of the {len(manifest)} bibliography entries, with the local "
        "copy where one may be stored and the reason where one may not.",
        "Generated by `src/fetch_sources.py`.", "",
        f"* Open-access full texts stored: **{counts['fulltext']}**",
        f"* Public-domain government documents stored: **{counts['document']}**",
        f"* Metadata and link only: **{counts['metadata'] + counts['unresolved']}**",
        "",
        "A missing copy is a licensing limit, not a gap in the record: the DOI, "
        "the URL and the resolved metadata are here for every entry, in "
        "`data/sources/metadata/`.", "",
        "| # | Entry | Identifier | Local copy | Why |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for row in manifest:
        ident = row["doi"] or row["url"] or "—"
        if len(ident) > 60:
            ident = ident[:57] + "…"
        who = (row["authors"] or "").split(",")[0]
        lines.append(
            f"| {row['key'].split('_')[0]} | {who} {row['year'] or ''} — "
            f"{row['title'][:70]} | `{ident}` | "
            f"{('`' + row['local_copy'] + '`') if row['local_copy'] else '—'} "
            f"| {row['why']} |")
    (OUT / "MANIFEST.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

    print(json.dumps(counts, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
PY

r=open('README.md').read()
anchor = "## Reading order for the results"

    python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt   # pinned; metapredict's version changes its predictions
    python3 src/uniprot_features.py              # self-test, must pass first
    python3 src/variance_decomposition.py        # the headline result

`src/README.md` gives the full run order and says which three scripts need
network access.

## What is stored here, and what could not be

The repository is meant to stand on its own. The sequences, the structures, the
metabolic models, the titre corpus, the bibliography, the figures, the
manuscript and the working transcripts are all in it.

| Path | What is in it |
|---|---|
| `data/sources/` | A local copy of every cited source that may be redistributed, and resolved metadata plus the DOI for every one that may not. `data/sources/MANIFEST.md` lists all 230 entries with the reason in each case. |
| `docs/history/` | The session transcripts that produced the work, redacted, and a readable work log derived from them. |

Where a paper is not stored, that is a licensing limit rather than a gap: the
DOI, the URL and the resolved metadata are recorded for it, which is what makes
the citation checkable.

input.command:
git -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com -c user.name=Claude commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
Pull the cited sources into the repository, with a manifest for the rest

A bibliography is a set of promises that someone else's server will still be
there. `src/fetch_sources.py` turns as much of it as licensing permits into
files here, and records, for every one of the 230 entries, either where the
local copy is or why there is not one.

* 45 open-access full texts, as PMC XML where there is a PMCID and the
  publisher's PDF otherwise;
* 6 US government documents (FDA letters, GRAS notices, a Federal Register
  item), which are not under copyright;
* 230 resolved metadata records, and an Internet Archive snapshot recorded
  beside the live URL for the 27 link-only entries that had one, because a
  company page is the kind of link that quietly disappears.

OpenAlex decides what may be stored: a Creative Commons or public-domain
licence is taken as permission, anything else is not, however freely the paper
can be read. It also supplies the PMCID, which is what lets this run in minutes
rather than hours — a Europe PMC title search takes twenty seconds.

Also pins the package versions every number was computed with. metapredict in
particular changes its predictions between major versions, so a bounded
requirement would not reproduce the disorder scores.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: [session link redacted]
